candidate.name: provider-support-source-20261106
candidate.qualification: Source and fixture candidate only; no release, installed-package, desktop, or hardware qualification.

baseline.scope: Source trace baseline only; not a release, install, hardware, or full candidate qualification.

phaseMeanings.ready: Observed provider readiness; null means not observed, and initialization alone is not readiness.
phaseMeanings.requested: A user or shell caller expressed intent.
phaseMeanings.accepted: The provider explicitly accepted dispatch. A shell-side queue or void call does not imply acceptance.
phaseMeanings.completed: A provider result or observed readback confirms the operation. Accepted asynchronous work alone is not complete.

supportBundleV1.providerObservation: Caller-supplied offline snapshot only; no live provider query is implied.

capabilities.uiEntry: Session menu, launcher actions, and shell lifecycle IPC.
operations: Allowlisted lock, logout, shutdown, reboot, suspend, hibernate, and firmware-reboot requests.
Observe whether hibernation is available.
requirements: Session observation and action dispatch are independently opt-in; the live shell must enable both before dispatch.
Windows itself decides whether a requested system action can proceed.

degradedExamples.case: The combined suspend-then-hibernate command is intentionally not implemented.
The native session component has not loaded or failed to load.

capabilities.operationCaveat: Native session methods return void. Report a dispatched action as requested only; the current interface cannot establish provider acceptance or completion.

capabilities.uiEntry: Settings > Window management, plus staged drag/drop preview.
capabilities.provider: Opt-in Quickshell Windows Tiling manager behind the staged Tiling service.
operations: Observe eligible top-level windows and layout state.
Interactive mode tiles only windows admitted by the configured rules; options include gaps, border colors, and drag/drop.
requirements: Tiling is off by default and must be explicitly enabled; Interactive mode is a separate choice from Observe.
A usable screen and an eligible application/window are required for a concrete tile.

degradedExamples.case: A session-owner conflict or empty eligibility policy refuses an enable request.
The native backend or screen observation is unavailable.
A concrete placement fails and is surfaced as a per-window failure.

capabilities.uiEntry: Bar audio popout, Settings > Audio, and volume hotkeys.
capabilities.provider: Quickshell Windows audio service backed by Windows audio endpoints and sessions.
operations: Observe default input/output and application streams.
Change supported endpoint selection, mute, and stream volume.
requirements: A usable Windows audio endpoint or application session is required for a non-empty model.
Input availability and output availability are independent.

degradedExamples.case: The backend initializes successfully but reports no usable audio endpoints or streams.
The backend cannot initialize or a default endpoint disappears.
A concrete control call reports a failure.

capabilities.uiEntry: Bar battery popout/status and its optional power-profile selector.
capabilities.provider: Quickshell Windows power-status and power-profile adapters.
operations: Observe battery/power status when Windows exposes a battery.
Observe a mapped effective power profile; optional profile writes require their separate gate and verified result.
requirements: Battery fields depend on an attached battery; desktops may have none.
Power-profile observations/writes are separately gated and only mapped profiles are exposed.

degradedExamples.case: A successful power-status read on a device with no battery is not a battery failure.
The provider cannot map a requested profile on this device/configuration.
A profile write was requested but did not receive a successful result/readback.

capabilities.uiEntry: Bar Bluetooth status/popout, Settings > Bluetooth, and radio toggle.
capabilities.provider: Quickshell Bluetooth WinRT adapter and the staged Bluetooth service.
operations: Observe adapters/devices, request discovery, connect/disconnect, and forget supported devices.
Pairing is explicit; PIN/passkey completion may be handed to Windows.
requirements: A functioning Windows Bluetooth adapter and radio are required; radio state and operation policy are separate.
A Windows-owned PIN/passkey prompt remains the authority when the provider requests it.

degradedExamples.case: No adapter is observed before the bounded first-scan deadline, or the native component fails.
The adapter/radio is blocked by hardware switch or policy.
A ready adapter reports no devices.
Radio or device state is changing or the Explorer/OS provider is recovering.

capabilities.uiEntry: Bar scroll actions and the per-screen OSD brightness control.
capabilities.provider: Quickshell Windows brightness service with a per-display route selected from observed target identity/capabilities.
operations: Read and request brightness changes for an identified screen where a safe route is available.
Possible backend methods include WMI, built-in LCD, DDC/CI, HDR SDR-white, and owned software dimming; these are conditional routes, not a universal monitor guarantee.
requirements: A screen-to-target correlation and a compatible device/driver route are required for hardware writes.
External DDC/CI availability and monitor range behavior vary by physical hardware.

degradedExamples.case: No safe brightness target or compatible write route can be established for a display.
The display/provider disappears or a query cannot be completed.
A routed write/readback reports failure; one monitor is not evidence for another.

capabilities.uiEntry: Network popout and Settings > Network > Wi-Fi.
capabilities.provider: Staged Windows NetworkService/Nmcli adapters over Quickshell Windows WLAN and connectivity providers.
operations: Observe Wi-Fi radio, interface, scan list, current connection and an available-network snapshot.
When controls are enabled, request radio changes, connect to a saved profile or open network, disconnect, forget, and rescan.
Ethernet is a connected/not-connected observation only; VPN and new protected profiles are owned by Windows Settings.
requirements: Nearby Wi-Fi listing can require Windows Location permission; denying it hides the list rather than preserving stale observations.
The native network observation/control environment gates are separate; read-only observation does not enable radio or connection writes.
Caelestia passes no Wi-Fi password and does not collect credentials. A new protected network opens Windows Settings.

degradedExamples.case: Windows Location access is denied for nearby-network enumeration.
WLAN initialization/subscription fails; no adapter is not reported as an empty network list.
WLAN is initializing, scanning, or connecting.
A completed, permission-valid refresh returns no visible access points.
Wired connection controls, VPN configuration, and profile creation are not implemented by this UI.

capabilities.uiEntry: Dashboard/lock media cards and media transport keybinds.
operations: Observe active Windows media sessions and supported per-session transport capabilities.
Send play/pause, next, previous, or stop only when the selected session advertises that operation.
requirements: Windows must expose a media session; a successful scan with no session is empty, not a provider failure.
Individual applications may not support every transport command.

degradedExamples.case: GSMTC is ready and no media sessions are active.
GSMTC initialization or session scan fails.
A selected media app does not expose the requested transport command.

capabilities.uiEntry: Notification center/sidebar and notification preference rows.
capabilities.provider: Quickshell Windows notification server; Windows toast mirroring is a separate consent-gated capability.
operations: Receive and render shell-local notifications, history, dismissal and fullscreen policy.
Optionally mirror Windows notifications after the user explicitly grants notification access.
requirements: Windows notification access must be explicitly requested by user action; denial or revocation disables mirroring but does not itself disable local shell notifications.
A usable notification server owner is required for local forwarding.

degradedExamples.case: The user denies Windows user-notification access or later revokes it.
Notification service ownership/initialization fails.
Windows has not answered a consent request or provider recovery is pending.
The service is healthy and there are no retained notifications.

capabilities.uiEntry: Bar workspaces/active-window widgets, global keybinds, and window-dispatch consumers.
capabilities.provider: Staged Hypr compatibility facade over Quickshell Windows foreground/window tracking, keyboard hooks, and optional virtual-desktop COM control.
operations: Observe tracked top-level windows, foreground application, keyboard layout/lock state, monitors and workspace state.
Allowlisted workspace switch/move and graceful WM_CLOSE dispatch when the applicable operation is enabled and supported.
requirements: Hypr observation and dispatch are separate opt-ins; dispatch needs both.
Workspace switch/move use supported virtual-desktop interface families 26100, 26200, or 26300 and require Explorer/provider availability.
The facade exposes one globally focused workspace, not independent per-monitor workspaces.

degradedExamples.case: A request outside the adapter allowlist is refused; special workspaces are consumed as no-ops.
The observation backend is disabled, has not initialized, or Explorer/provider is disconnected.
Windows refuses a workspace/window move.
Explorer or a desktop-control provider is restarting.

capabilities.operationCaveat: The native dispatch method returns void; a sent request is not a confirmed window/workspace result.

capabilities.uiEntry: PrintScreen, Win+Shift+S, Win+Shift+R, launcher actions, and the recording card.
capabilities.provider: First-party caelestia-capture.exe from windows/capture, managed by Caelestia.Windows.CaptureHost and the compatibility-named Glazier/Recorder adapters.
operations: Launch the first-party screenshot picker/editor after shell surfaces are dismissed.
Start, stop, pause/resume, and observe capture recording states and finalized-file ownership.
requirements: The live installed shell, bundled executable and interactive desktop are required; smoke/read-only profiles suppress process launch.
Executable-path availability does not prove a running host, accepted command, completed screenshot, or saved recording.

degradedExamples.case: The bundled executable cannot be resolved or a known process/status client fails.
The host is starting, shell surfaces are still hiding, a command is queued, or a recording is finalizing.
The provider reports an error or a recording start is not confirmed before its bounded deadline.
The provider is healthy and no recording is active.

capabilities.operationCaveat: Screenshot launch is asynchronous. A shell return value/accepted detached launch is not a file-completion result; use provider status/journal evidence for recording state.
capabilities.captureMigration: Maintained source and managed identity are integrated at the capture source revision. The Glazier origin revision remains attribution/provenance, not the active source revision. Exact-pair, installed-package and live capture acceptance remain separate.

capabilities.provider: Quickshell Windows execution-state/power-request backend through the staged IdleHold facade.
operations: Acquire and release a Windows system/display idle-inhibition request.
requirements: Only a user-enabled live shell requests inhibition; read-only/offscreen modes do not change power state.

degradedExamples.case: Windows power request acquisition fails; the card shows a provider error.
A release fails; the held state remains visible rather than claiming inhibition ended.

capabilities.uiEntry: Bar keyboard-layout popout and global shortcut handling.
capabilities.provider: Quickshell Windows keyboard/layout APIs behind the staged Hypr and shortcut adapters.
operations: Observe the foreground application's input layout and lock keys.
List installed input profiles and request a layout switch for the validated target application.
requirements: Layout observation is per foreground input thread; a valid target window is needed for switching.
TSF and registered-layout fallback behavior can differ for IMEs and substituted profiles.

degradedExamples.case: The installed layout profile cannot be resolved or the target application/window is no longer valid.
A substituted or handle-less profile cannot be switched through the available target API.
The foreground application or its input thread changes during the request.

capabilities.uiEntry: Bar notification-area tray, item activation, and native context menus.
capabilities.provider: Quickshell Windows SystemTray hook/host projected by the staged WindowsTray adapter.
operations: Observe eligible notification-area items when the tray interceptor is enabled.
Activate items and open their native menus only when the hook capability and activation policy permit it.
requirements: Explorer and the native tray hook must be available; observation and activation are separate gates.
The native item uses Windows-owned menus, not the inherited Linux semantic menu model.

degradedExamples.case: The hook is unavailable or never reaches ready; tray items are not claimed observable.
Explorer restarts and the tray host is reconnecting.
A ready tray host reports no eligible icons.

capabilities.uiEntry: Settings > Wallpaper and style, wallpaper file picker, and desktop background.
capabilities.provider: Staged Wallpapers orchestration over Quickshell Windows wallpaper/background APIs; WallpaperEngine is a separate optional underlay participant.
operations: Select a local wallpaper and apply its background/palette behavior.
Observe the desktop host/underlay handoff when an external wallpaper owner is present.
requirements: The Windows interactive desktop and current wallpaper host ownership determine which background route can be applied.
Dynamic scheme generation is optional and depends on the configured local generator/runtime.

degradedExamples.case: The selected screen, wallpaper host, or optional scheme generator is unavailable.
The desktop owner/underlay is being rediscovered or handed back.
No wallpaper has been selected for a screen.

capabilities.uiEntry: Clipboard picker opened by the named caelestia:clipboard action/IPC after the user configures a binding.
capabilities.provider: Caelestia.Windows.WindowsClipboard plugin over Windows' own WinRT clipboard history; no parallel shell capture store.
operations: Refresh/read history, request bounded previews, paste, remove, clear, and open Windows clipboard settings.
requirements: The feature setting is enabled, Windows clipboard history is on, and Windows permits this user's history access.
The default profile ships no clipboard key binding; a user may bind Super+V, replacing Windows' own Win+V flyout for that chord.
Caelestia never enables Windows clipboard history itself.

degradedExamples.case: Windows refuses history access.
The native plugin/component fails to load.
History is healthy but contains no visible items, including when Windows history is off.

capabilities.supportBundleNote: The support-bundle v1 provider list has no clipboard ID. Do not add a synthetic clipboard row or imply that its provider health is currently exported. Never put clipboard content or preview material into support diagnostics.
